result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers propose deterministic tiering, RBAC enforcement, blast-radius resolution and approvals bound to the exact command. B is stronger: it says outright that fatigue has made the human tap only a nominal control. It also adds a digest of auto-run actions with per-item Undo and feedback controls, plus a today-versus-redesign safety comparison. A only logs and posts thread notices with an undo hint, so its review and reversal path is thinner. Neither offers true task-scoped grants with a time limit, and neither invents incident statistics. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers spot approval fatigue, sort actions into tiers by risk, enforce limits with RBAC and require each approval to match a hash of the exact command. A is stronger on rubric item 5: its per-shift digest gives every auto-run action its own Undo, puts doubtful items first and lists blocked or skipped actions. B only logs actions and posts an undo hint in a thread. Neither answer offers true task- or time-limited grants that expire, though B's short-lived tokens come a little closer.
